pages.text: Geolosys names each deposit after its $(bold)mineral$(), the real name of that ore in the ground. The mineral tells you the metal: there is no iron ore block, there is hematite.$(br2)Shallow to deep. The next three entries give each ore: what it drops, where, and what it is for.

pages.title: Shallow

pages.title: Deep, everywhere

pages.text: $(bold)No two deposits are alike.$() Most are the usual size; about a third are small pockets, worth a quarter to a half of that; about one in ten is a $(bold)big strike$() of two to three times the usual. A small find is not the whole region's luck.$(br2)Deposits only replace stone, so a cave, a dirt bank or the surface takes its bite: what you dig out is often less than the deposit was.

$(bold)Mining:$() ore drops $(bold)clusters$(), never raw ore; deepslate metal ore drops one to two. $(bold)Fortune$() gives more clusters. $(bold)Silk Touch$() gives the ore block itself.$(br2)$(bold)Processing:$() a cluster smelts to one ingot. A millstone or crushing wheels crush it, and washing (an encased fan through water) turns crushed ore into nuggets with a bonus. Uranium is not in this world.
